questions.prompt: What is the main difference between cash-game chips and tournament chips?

choices.text: Cash chips represent real money you can leave with; tournament chips are only tournament equity.
Tournament chips are always worth more dollars than cash chips.
Cash chips expire at the end of each orbit; tournament chips do not.
There is no meaningful difference once blinds are posted.

questions.explanation: In cash, your stack is withdrawable value. In tournaments, chips only buy tournament equity and cannot be cashed mid-event.

questions.prompt: In a typical live cash game, when can you leave the table?

choices.text: Only after you win a big pot.
Generally anytime between hands (house rules permitting).
Only when the tournament clock hits a break.
Never until the dealer forces a table change.

questions.explanation: Cash games are continuous and optional: you can usually stand up when a hand ends, subject to room etiquette and rules.

questions.prompt: How do blinds usually behave in live cash versus tournaments?

choices.text: Cash blinds escalate every few minutes; tournament blinds stay fixed forever.
Both formats keep identical blind schedules for fairness.
Cash blinds stay at fixed stakes; tournament blinds escalate on a clock.
Live cash has no blinds; only tournaments use blinds.

questions.explanation: A $1/$2 cash game stays $1/$2. Tournament structures raise blinds over time, forcing shorter stacks and rising pressure.

questions.prompt: If you lose your whole stack in a live cash game, what usually happens next?

choices.text: You are eliminated from the casino for the day.
You may rebuy (or leave); the game continues without a tournament finish.
You automatically win the next hand as compensation.
The dealer converts your empty seat into a tournament bubble.

questions.explanation: Busting in cash ends that buy-in, not the event. You can buy back in or walk away; there is no payout ladder.

questions.prompt: Why do live cash stacks often play deeper than late-stage tournament stacks?

choices.text: Because cash games ban raises larger than 2 big blinds.
Because players can keep reloading while blinds stay fixed, so effective stacks stay deep.
Because live cash never uses a button or blinds.
Because tournaments always start with more chips than cash games.

questions.explanation: Fixed blinds plus optional reloads keep many cash tables deep. Escalating tournament blinds shrink stacks as the event progresses.
